candidate.answerReason: The nickels cause a 20x-cent overcount, while the dimes cause a 9x-cent undercount. The net overcount is 11x cents.

methods.label: Track the two counting errors
methods.explanation:
Only the miscounted coins affect the correction. Each nickel counted as a quarter contributes \(25-5=20\) cents too much, so the \(x\) nickels make the total \(20x\) cents too high.

Each dime counted as a cent contributes \(10-1=9\) cents too little, so the \(x\) dimes make the total \(9x\) cents too low. Together, the errors leave the recorded total
\[
20x-9x=11x
\]
cents too high. The clerk must therefore subtract \(\boxed{11x\text{ cents}}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{C}}\). This formula also gives zero correction when \(x=0\).
methods.levelReason: The argument uses elementary coin values and the subtraction of two linear expressions.

candidate.annotationRationale: The target is modeling and interpreting a net correction with an algebraic sum-difference expression. Writing the two error amounts and combining their like terms support this method. The correctly counted coins need not be included.
